central_rq: When do users ask for more information instead of accepting the initial explanation?
scope: Qualitative Information-Seeking sub-study after Trust Calibration; target 12 participants.

qualitative_analysis.target_logic: Pattern saturation / qualitative coverage rather than statistical power.

ethics.notes: Covered by the same internal research-team ethics/data-protection self-assessment as Phase 16. No institutional approval or exemption is claimed.

participant_materials.consent_text:
# Participant Information Sheet — AwareML Main Study

**Study:** AwareML Trust Calibration and Human Oversight Study  
**Institution:** University of Tartu, Institute of Computer Science  
**Research contact:** Vikash Maheshwari — maheshwari@ut.ee

## Purpose
This study investigates whether people calibrate trust in AI-generated explanations appropriately, especially whether trust decreases when an explanation is factually incorrect, and when users seek additional evidence before relying on an AutoML recommendation.

## What you will do
You will evaluate 20 AI explanation items. Each item contains a task, an AI explanation and reference evidence. Some explanations may intentionally contain factual or reasoning errors. You will rate trust, perceived factual correctness, fluency and confident-sounding language, and choose whether you would **Accept**, **Override** or **Reject** the explanation. You may also complete a short questionnaire about human control, explanation usefulness and study usability.

A smaller optional Information-Seeking activity may ask you to inspect additional evidence or ask follow-up questions before making a final recommendation decision.

## Eligibility and voluntariness
Participants must be at least 18 years old. Participation is voluntary. You may stop at any time without penalty and without giving a reason. Participants who helped author the Track-1 scenario/stimulus bank should not take part in this study.

## Data collected
AwareML stores a pseudonymous participant/session identifier, expertise group and self-rating, study responses, response times, Accept/Override/Reject decisions, questionnaire answers, and—if you take part in Information Seeking—follow-up categories, evidence views, timing, final decision and task rationale. The study is designed not to place names or raw dataset rows in the study response store.

## Risks and benefits
This is assessed by the research team as a minimal-risk behavioral study. Possible burdens include mild fatigue, uncertainty when judging deliberately imperfect explanations, or frustration when comparing evidence. There is no guaranteed direct personal benefit. The research may contribute to safer and more human-centred AutoML systems.

## Confidentiality
Study responses are stored under pseudonymous identifiers and are accessible only to the research team. Participant-facing records are kept separate from researcher-only ground-truth labels. Main Study response data must not be sent as raw participant data to external generative-AI services. Results will be reported in aggregate form; illustrative quotations, if used, will be de-identified.

## Retention and withdrawal
Research data are planned to be retained for five years after publication of the associated AwareML journal article and then deleted or irreversibly anonymized, subject to University of Tartu record-management requirements. You may request withdrawal of linkable pseudonymous study data by providing your participant code before the data are irreversibly anonymized or aggregated so that the record can no longer be linked back to you.

## Data controller and contacts
The data controller is the University of Tartu.  
Study questions: **maheshwari@ut.ee**  
Data-protection questions: **andmekaitse@ut.ee**  
Research-ethics questions: **eetikakomitee@ut.ee**
participant_materials.instructions: You will start from a standardized measured AwareML recommendation. Ask only the follow-up questions you genuinely need. You may inspect performance, fairness, sustainability, drift or explainability evidence; compare alternatives; challenge the recommendation; request clarification; or stop immediately if you already have enough information. Zero follow-ups is a valid behavior. Finish by recording whether you would Accept, Override or Reject the recommendation.

study_context.pilot_policy: Researcher may capture one standardized measured AwareML run plus observed Decision Lab ranking for repeated participant sessions.
study_context.main_policy: Use a frozen standardized study context; real participants should not be required to rerun Run Studio unless that is explicitly part of the approved design.
